audit.chain: hash = sha256(prev_hash | canonical_payload); edit of any row breaks every subsequent link
audit.covered_by_reconciliation: all reads/access; sweep anchored on the nginx access log (independent), not the app middleware
audit.mutation_atomicity: audit row commits in the SAME transaction as the mutation; a commit without its audit row is a transaction failure
audit.omission_detection: sweep replays nginx access log vs audit_events by request_id; a missing mutation row fails
audit.tamper_detection: edit a middle row => chain verification fails

backwards_compat: WS-3 X-Pakhi-Key flow, error envelope, rate-limit headers, X-Pakhi-Edge-Status, and backtest client_id semantics keep working unchanged for existing keys; CI re-runs the full WS-3 suite against every WS-4 change
gate: explicit user infra-first decision (recorded in WS4_PROGRESS.md); G1 is UNDER-POWERED, WS-4 is infrastructure never an edge claim

human.refresh: opaque, rotating, hashed at rest; rotation revokes the old token; reuse of a revoked token revokes the whole family

identity.machine: X-Pakhi-Key, SHA-256 hashed at rest; per-tenant keys in Postgres with pk_live_/pk_test_ prefixes; env/file source retained as bootstrap/admin-only

reconciliation_anchor: nginx access log, written outside the app code path, with request_id propagated through the proxy; nginx config ships in T4 (no proxy exists in the repo today)

roles.admin: operator + tenant management, human-user management, audit-log read, paper-ledger read

roles.operator: viewer + own-tenant backtests + own-tenant key management; default grant for machine keys

secrets.boot_gate: missing or weak PAKHI_JWT_SECRET (or equal to a documented test default) refuses startup; never a silent runtime default
secrets.ci: secret-scan step + tree-walk test asserting no pk_live_-prefixed or PAKHI_JWT_SECRET=<value> leaks
secrets.tenant_keys: SHA-256 hashed in Postgres; only prefix stored/returned; plaintext shown exactly once at creation

tenancy.isolation: query-layer WHERE tenant_id = :tid injected by get_tenant_scope; missing scope filter fails a test; cross-tenant reads return 404/403

tiers_scope: token bucket stays in-memory, thread-safe, single-worker only; multi-worker bucket state is WS-5/Redis
uptime: conditional offer: 99.9% availability is offered to paying customers only while the WS-5 reliability machinery is live AND the 30-day measurement window is open and recorded; single-worker remains the documented posture; no achieved-uptime claim until the window elapses and evidence accrues
_amended: 2026-08-14 T6 (WS-5): no-SLA clause upgraded to a CONDITIONAL offer — 99.9% is offered only while the WS-5 machinery is live (Redis multi-worker fail-closed, metrics, SLO accounting + status page, green DR drill) AND the 30-day measurement window is open and recorded. The offer's evidence accrues during the window; Pakhi never fabricates an achieved uptime number (G1 remains UNDER-POWERED).
